Sunderdeep · pass six · part two · docs/renovation

Light & Stone

Part one made the floor sound: bodies that keep their distance, three-wide corridors, watertight walls, dressed rooms, biome chests and spell icons. Part two makes it feel real:

  • high walls with rock crowns and dressing
  • light that matters to a dice roll
  • fog over what the party hasn't seen
  • foes that wait in their halls
  • pools and lava lakes
  • biome gates
  • status marks and damage numbers
  • a camp where every companion has a place

That is seventeen phases, each with a gate.

§

The plan

order, and why that order
first · the rules of the world (sim)1 → 5

These phases change what the dice see:

  • Bodies stop entering walls.
  • Pools change the terrain.
  • Torches move into the sim so light can change a hit.
  • Foes wait until they are found.
  • The party remembers what it has seen.

Everything drawn afterwards reads these.

then · the stone6 → 11

In order:

  • sprites stop being cut by the wall behind them
  • walls grow high again, cut down only near the party
  • their tops become rock
  • their faces get dressed
  • the furniture catalogue grows biome by biome, with shadow and light
  • the stairs become a gate
then · the readouts, the camp, the gates12 → 17

In order:

  • light and status marks on every body
  • damage and heal numbers that actually show
  • the fallen stay fallen
  • O1 icons in the log
  • the camp rebuilt with companion plots
  • every gate run again, and the records

1

Walls hold

sim/combat · sim/dungeon · every mover
Cause

Movement tests a point, never a body. moveToward steps straight at the next waypoint without asking whether the step lands on floor, and A*'s smoothed segments can shave a corner. separate() slides a push along x or y, and each axis on its own may be open.

A body's centre can therefore sit a hair from a wall cell, and its sprite (a third of a hex wide) is then drawn half inside the wall. Post-fight drift and spawns use the same point test.

Change
  • One clear(x, y, r) on the floor: the point and six points on a circle of radius r must all be open.
  • Every mover (hero, monster, drift, separation, spawn, start spot, corpse) moves only to a clear position, sliding along the wall when blocked.
  • Spawns and start spots choose clear cell centres only.
Gate
A new test and measure line: across 3 seeds × 10 simulated minutes, sampled every tick, no living body centre is closer than 0.22 to a closed cell and no body ever stands on one. Before and after are both recorded.
2

Pools & lakes

sim/dungeon/generate/pools · data/pools
What

Some rooms and wide corridors get a pool: an irregular blob of a new LIQUID tile. It cannot be walked on, sight passes over it, and connectivity is re-verified for every cell it takes. The liquid is the biome's:

  • Cisterns: still water
  • Ossuary: black bog
  • Fungal Reach: spore-scummed mire
  • Cinderworks: lava
  • Drowned Vault: deep water
  • Rimehollow: frozen mere
  • Sable Court: ink
  • Wyrm Deeps: magma
Draw
  • The pool sits recessed, with a shoreline ring of wet stone.
  • The liquid surface is a slow shader: ambient, less than one cycle a second.
  • Lava and magma are light sources (phase 3).
Gate
Connectivity holds on 200 floors. No pool lies on a door, the entry, the stairs or an interactable. A shot per biome.
3

Light

sim/light · data/light · combat/attack
What

A light map per floor, in the sim, so the dice see it. The sources are:

  • wall torches, which move from the renderer into the sim so both agree where they burn
  • braziers and candles among the furniture
  • lava and magma pools
  • burning surfaces
  • a small lamp the party carries

Each cell reads well lit, half lit or dark.

Rule

An attack roll against a target in darkness −3, in half light ±0, in full light +2. It applies to both sides.

Spells with saves are unaffected: light changes being hit. The numbers are a starting point, and simulate decides.

Draw
The floor, walls and every sprite take the light map's tint, so a lit room reads as lit and a dark corner as dark. The Lambert point-light pool stays for the warm fall-off.
Gate
  • A test that the to-hit modifier applies in each state.
  • Simulate median depth within ±10% of phase 2's figure, reported either side.
  • Census all in band.
4

Waiting foes

sim/combat/Encounter · targeting
Cause
A monster targets the nearest hero anywhere on the floor and walks at it (aggro radius 7.5, no line of sight asked). A whole floor converges on the entry.
Change
  • A monster is dormant in its room until one of these happens:
    • a hero it can see comes within 6
    • a hero enters its room
    • it is hurt
  • Waking alerts its room.
  • The party goes to them: heroes pick targets only among foes they can see. Otherwise they walk to the nearest room still holding foes, the way post-fight drift walks to chests.
Gate
A measure line: foes that moved before any hero came within 6 and in sight = 0. Simulate within ±10%; census in band.
5

Fog of war

sim/dungeon/explore · render/tiles/fog
What

The floor tracks explored cells: anything a hero has had in sight within 7 cells.

  • Unseen ground is black: walls, floor, furniture, all of it.
  • Explored ground stays drawn: walls, furniture, pools, chests and the gate. Foes there are hidden unless a hero sees them now.
  • A foe shows only while in current sight.
  • Corpses and loot stay where they were seen.
How
  • The sim sets bits per cell each tick. This is cheap: only the party's sight disc is recast when the party moves a cell.
  • The renderer keeps a fog texture (one texel per cell) that floor, walls, props and actors sample, with a soft two-cell edge.
  • The minimap-free UI needs nothing else.
Gate
A four-shot sequence: entry, first corridor, first room, cleared floor. Tests: no hidden foe drawn, and explored never shrinks.
6

Sprite depth

render/engine/billboard · Dressing · ActorView

A billboard is a camera-facing quad. Its top leans back into the room behind it, so the wall behind a tall bookshelf or a hero cuts its top off. That is the "cut off at the edges" in the shots.

The fix is one shader for every sprite (furniture, chests, loot, figures, gates) that writes the depth of its foot for the whole quad. The wall behind can never cut it; a wall in front still hides what it should.

GateShots of shelves and figures against back walls in every biome, whole. A figure behind a wall stays hidden.
7

High walls

render/tiles/wallMass · HexMesher
What
  • Walls stand 1.7 high (was 1.0).
  • Part one cut every near-side wall to a stub. Now every wall is high, and only the walls between the camera and the party, within a radius of the party, sink to a stub. The shader does this smoothly as the party walks.
  • "Keep most of them high", and the fight is never hidden.
Watertight
Faces are emitted wherever two cells could differ once sunk, so a sunk wall still has faces round it. The measure tool re-checks with the party placed at every room centre.
Gate
0 unfaced steps and 0 void edges, sunk and unsunk. Shots.
8

Rock crowns

render/tiles · gen/textures

The tops stop being flat. Rock beyond the first ring rises and falls from cell to cell: each cell's height varies, and its top is faceted, with the centre raised or split into crags. It gets a per-biome stone texture:

  • Cisterns: moss seams
  • Ossuary: bone in the rock
  • Fungal Reach: caps sprouting
  • Cinderworks: ember cracks
  • Drowned Vault: wet dark
  • Rimehollow: rime caps
  • Sable Court: cut black stone
  • Wyrm Deeps: scorched
The first ring keeps its masonry coping, with broken merlons.

Stalagmite props stand on some tops. Because every cell keeps its own prism, varied heights still get faces.

GateThe measure tool stays at 0 / 0. 8 biome shots looked at.

Pieces hang on the visible wall faces at a set density, chosen by biome from a data table (R3):

  • Cisterns: pipes, sluice wheels, algae
  • Ossuary: skull niches, bone garlands
  • Fungal Reach: shelf fungus, root curtains
  • Cinderworks: chains, bellows, glowing seams
  • Drowned Vault: nets, barnacles, drip streaks
  • Rimehollow: icicles, rime
  • Sable Court: tapestries, portraits, sconces
  • Wyrm Deeps: claw scores, hung scales

Shields and weapon trophies appear everywhere.

Furniture, grown

data/dressing · gen/sprites/props · furniture.html

The catalogue gains shared pieces:

  • pillar, statue, rug, stool, pots, wine rack, shelf, cage, rope coil, well

Each biome also gets at least five pieces of its own, made in its own materials:

  • Cisterns: sluice gate, water barrel, pipe junction, drain grate, bucket stack
  • Ossuary: bone throne, ossuary shelf, coffin, skull pile, reliquary
  • Fungal Reach: giant cap, spore pod, rotting log, fungus shelf, root knot
  • Cinderworks: anvil, forge, coal cart, quench trough, chain hoist
  • Drowned Vault: anchor, net rack, coral, boat hull, kelp
  • Rimehollow: ice crystal, frozen barrel, fur rack, sled, snow drift
  • Sable Court: throne, statue, candelabrum, long table, carpet
  • Wyrm Deeps: dragon ribs, egg clutch, hoard heap, scorched pillar, claw-marked slab

Every prop gets a contact shadow and takes the light map's tint (phase 3).

furniture.html shows every piece, in every state and every biome, drawn by the game's own generator.

GateThe showcase page is built and looked at. Room shots in 8 biomes. Draw calls stay one per floor for all furniture.
11

Biome gates

the stairs, remade

The stair well becomes a gate: a voxel arch in the biome's own stone, over a portal surface animated by a shader (a slow swirl, with motes rising). It lights its surroundings. Eight designs:

  • Cisterns: a sluice arch over falling water
  • Ossuary: a rib arch over grave-light
  • Fungal Reach: a cap-ringed hollow over spore-glow
  • Cinderworks: an iron furnace mouth
  • Drowned Vault: a coral ring over a tide-pool
  • Rimehollow: an ice arch
  • Sable Court: a black-stone door with pale light
  • Wyrm Deeps: a jawbone gate over magma

None of them is gold.

GateShots of all 8 gates.
12

Status marks

gen/art/status · ActorView

Beside every body, above the ring, sits a small row of pixel marks, generated on the O1 grammar. First comes its light state: a full sun (well lit), a half sun (half lit) or a closed eye (dark). Then its conditions:

  • wet, burning, chilled, frozen, poisoned, prone, restrained
  • blessed, marked, charmed, frightened, hasted, cursed

Each condition keeps its fixed hue plus a mark, as the damage types do.

GateAn icon sheet on the showcase page. A shot with marks on heroes and foes.
13

Damage numbers

render/vfx/FloatingText

FloatingText exists but no screenshot has ever shown a number, so first find why. Then:

  • red for damage taken, green for healing, a larger ember-white for a critical
  • set in the game's type, with a dark outline
  • rising a third of a hex and fading in 0.9 s
  • kept in reduced motion, which motion-and-feedback Q4 already keeps
GateA burst of shots showing numbers on both sides.

16

The camp

campLayout · CampScene
Ground
  • A larger camp with a palisade of stakes, paving round the fire, and trodden paths.
  • Built with the dungeon's own pieces: rock-crowned outcrops, dressing and light map.
  • The fire is the main light source, with lanterns on the stalls.
Stalls

Six stalls spread round the ring, each dressed by its trade:

  • Chronicler: lectern, ledgers, candles
  • weaponsmith: forge, anvil, rack
  • armourer: mannequin, mail, shields
  • alchemist: still, shelves of flasks
  • arcanist: crystal, scroll case, rune circle
  • tinkerer: gears, workbench
Companions

Each hero gets a plot dressed by background (twelve kits, data) and stands in front of it, for example:

  • soldier: tent and weapon rack
  • acolyte: shrine
  • sage: desk and books
  • noble: pavilion
  • outlander: pelts and a drying rack
Fire
A stone ring, logs, a spit and pot, log seats and ember motes. It lights the whole centre.
GateCamp shots. ui-checks. Every stall tap opens its shop. A kit sheet on the showcase page.
